title: A source whose page moved is re-pointed by kbid.py repoint, which writes the new row, supersedes the old one and re-keys its anchor and doc2query rows
goal: kbid.py repoint OLD_ID NEW_URL --root R re-points a moved source in one command that needs no registry licence record: a new _sources.csv row for the new url takes the old row's licence, reuse and publisher, the old row gets superseded_by, the citing facts' tags move to the new id and their anchor and doc2query rows are re-keyed so check.py and doc2query.py stale stay clean

run:
import csv, io, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbid, kbroot, kbfacts
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
d = os.path.join(t, "zq")
old_url, new_url = "https://example.org/docs/old-page", "https://example.org/docs/new-page"
old, new = kbid.source_id(old_url, "ZQ"), kbid.source_id(new_url, "ZQ")
fact = "The setting is on by default. [DOC %s]"
art = ["---", "topic: win/a", "priority: P1", "applies_to: x", "retrieved_utc: 2026-01-01", "sources: [" + old + "]", "status: complete", "---", "", "# A", "",
       "## Summary", "- Summary line one. [DOC " + old + "]", "", "## Facts", "- " + fact % old, ""]
files = {"_root.md": kbroot.root_md("zq", "ZQ", "internal", "planted"), **{k: v.format(name="zq") for k, v in kbroot.FILES.items()},
         "win/a.md": "\n".join(art)}
files["_sources.csv"] += old + "," + old_url + ",Old page,Example Org,CC BY 4.0 (planted),quote,2026-01-01,,,win/a.md,\n"
okey = kbfacts.fact_key(fact % old)
files["_anchors.csv"] = "fact,path,source_id,status,heading,terms,sha,quote,verified_utc\n" + okey + ",win/a.md," + old + ",unlocated:no-match,,,,,2026-01-01\n"
files["_retrieval/doc2query/expansions.csv"] = "key,question\n" + okey + ",Is the setting on by default?\n"
for rel, text in files.items():
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(d, rel)) or d, exist_ok=True)
    open(os.path.join(d, rel), "w", newline="").write(text)
env = dict(os.environ, KB_ROOTS=d)
run = lambda *a: subprocess.run([sys.executable, *a], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
r = run("_tools/kbid.py", "repoint", old, new_url, "--root", "zq")
rd = lambda p: open(os.path.join(d, p), newline="").read()
rows = {x["id"]: x for x in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(rd("_sources.csv")))}
nk = kbfacts.fact_key(fact % new)
bad = []
if old not in rows or rows[old]["superseded_by"] != new:
    bad.append("old row not superseded_by the new id")
n = rows.get(new, {})
if n.get("url") != new_url or (n.get("licence"), n.get("reuse"), n.get("publisher")) != ("CC BY 4.0 (planted)", "quote", "Example Org"):
    bad.append("new row missing or without the old licence, reuse and publisher")
if "- " + fact % new not in rd("win/a.md") or old in rd("win/a.md").split("## Facts")[1]:
    bad.append("the citing fact's tag is not moved to the new id")
if nk not in rd("_anchors.csv") or okey in rd("_anchors.csv"):
    bad.append("anchor row not re-keyed")
if nk not in rd("_retrieval/doc2query/expansions.csv") or okey in rd("_retrieval/doc2query/expansions.csv"):
    bad.append("doc2query row not re-keyed")
for cmd in (("_tools/check.py", "--root", "zq"), ("_tools/doc2query.py", "stale")):
    c = run(*cmd)
    if c.returncode:
        bad.append(cmd[1] + " exits " + str(c.returncode))
print("repoint exit", r.returncode, r.stderr[-200:], bad)
sys.exit(1 if r.returncode or bad else 0)

gates.question: What does the new row of kbid.py repoint carry as retrieved_utc and version_or_date, given the command reads no page?
options: old row's retrieved_utc, version_or_date names the old id
today's date and the old row's version_or_date
gates.recommendation: old row's retrieved_utc, version_or_date names the old id
gates.reason: the command fetched nothing, so a new date would claim a read that did not happen
gates.answer: old row's retrieved_utc, version_or_date names the old id

gates.question: Does kbid.py repoint re-verify the moved facts' anchors on the new page, and which citations does it move?
options: no page read: anchor rows keep status and verified_utc, only articles' tags move, other citing units are reported
fetch the new page and re-anchor
gates.recommendation: no page read: anchor rows keep status and verified_utc, only articles' tags move, other citing units are reported
gates.reason: the command stays offline and the follow-up is factdiff.py anchor --source
gates.answer: no page read: anchor rows keep status and verified_utc, only articles' tags move, other citing units are reported

gates.question: Where does the re-pointing code live, and does a repeat run converge?
options: kbid.repoint_source, with factdiff.rekey (new also= argument) reached inside the function; the same url again finishes a stopped run
gates.recommendation: kbid.repoint_source, with factdiff.rekey (new also= argument) reached inside the function; the same url again finishes a stopped run
gates.reason: the goal names kbid.py repoint and add_source's consumers stay unchanged
gates.answer: kbid.repoint_source, with factdiff.rekey (new also= argument) reached inside the function; the same url again finishes a stopped run

notes: Found 2026-11-09 when two refresh runs re-pointed 20 moved sources by hand with scratch scripts for 60 anchor and 15 doc2query rows, and kbid.py add refused hosts with no registry licence record. Premise: the planted-root check exits 1 on 55dde769f (no repoint subcommand). The command is registered in kbid.py main; its Use: docstring line and kbtools catalog follow.
